subject.title: Feature: browser upload tool fallback for non-standard file inputs (ByteUploader)

question: Should Browser upload grow an explicit custom-uploader file-injection mode, and if so should it be drop, paste, native drag, or a narrower API?
rationale: The implementation would intentionally send managed local file bytes through page-controlled event handlers outside the standard file-input boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API or security semantics.

options.title: Add explicit drop-file mode
options.body: Create a named Browser upload mode with managed-path validation, clear docs, focused tests, and live custom-uploader proof rather than silently falling back from upload.

options.title: Keep standard upload only
options.body: Reject custom uploader injection until there is stronger live evidence or a broader browser automation API design.

options.title: Defer to plugin/API design
options.body: Treat ByteUploader support as a future Browser plugin API discussion instead of an issue-ready implementation task.

recommendation.title: Add explicit drop-file mode
recommendation.body: Create a named Browser upload mode with managed-path validation, clear docs, focused tests, and live custom-uploader proof rather than silently falling back from upload.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail points to Browser plugin ownership and upload-route work by steipete.
